trend-to-content.name: Trend to content
trend-to-content.description: Give it a trend. BOSS researches the context, says honestly whether it is yours to talk about, and writes a script — which you read before anything is made.

trend.title: Trend
examples: Everyone is posting their AI coding setup

assess_brief.title: Assessment brief
assess_brief.description: Optional; leave blank for the stored relevance brief.
examples:
Decide whether this trend is worth us saying anything about. From the research below:
  WHAT IT IS: two sentences, for somebody who has not seen it.
  OURS OR NOT: say plainly whether we have standing to talk about this, and why.
  THE ANGLE: what we could say that is not what everyone else is saying. If there is nothing, say 'no angle' — that is a useful answer and a generic take is not.
  HOW LONG IT LASTS: is this a week or a day?
Do not manufacture relevance. Most trends are not ours, and saying so saves a video.

script_brief.title: Script brief
script_brief.description: Optional; leave blank for the stored script brief.
examples: Write a script for a short vertical video, 45 seconds at most, from the angle below. Open with the thing that makes somebody stop scrolling — not a greeting, not the channel name. Plain spoken sentences, the way a person talks. Mark where a caption or a diagram would help as [ON SCREEN: ...]. End with one specific thing to do or think about, never 'like and subscribe'. If the assessment said there is no angle, write one line saying so instead of a script.

sales-signal.name: Sales signal
sales-signal.description: Give it a company. BOSS researches them, scores the opportunity against what you sell, drafts an approach, and holds it for the salesperson to read.

salesperson.title: Salesperson email
salesperson.description: Internal recipient for the assessment and draft.

assess_brief.title: Assessment brief
assess_brief.description: Optional; leave blank for the stored scoring brief.
examples:
You are scoring a sales opportunity for a salesperson who will read this in thirty seconds. From the research below, write:
  FIT: a score out of 10 and one sentence saying what it rests on.
  WHY NOW: anything in the research that makes this a good moment, or 'nothing found'.
  RISKS: what would make this a waste of their time.
  UNKNOWNS: what the research did not establish.
Name the specific source-backed fact a first email could mention. Do not infer budget, headcount or intent that is not in the material. A confident guess is worse than a gap, because the salesperson will repeat it to the prospect.

draft_brief.title: Draft brief
draft_brief.description: Optional; leave blank for the stored draft brief.
examples: Prepare one note for the salesperson with two labeled sections: ASSESSMENT and DRAFT TO EDIT. In ASSESSMENT, faithfully summarize the fit, why now, risks, and unknowns from the assessment below. In DRAFT TO EDIT, write a short first email to the company, grounded only in a specific fact named in that assessment. No flattery, no 'I hope this finds you well', no invented mutual connections. Four sentences at most, with a question they can answer in one line. If there is no specific fact, say why a personalized email cannot yet be drafted rather than writing a generic one.

weekly-newsletter.name: Weekly newsletter
weekly-newsletter.description: Research the sectors you care about, write them up as a newsletter, and email it once you have read it.

sectors.title: Sectors to research
sectors.description: Topics to cover, in the order you want them.

brief.title: Writing brief
brief.description: Optional; leave blank for the stored house brief.
examples: Write a short weekly newsletter from the research below. One section per sector, in the order given. Three or four items per section, each a sentence or two, with the source named. Lead each section with whatever actually matters rather than whatever is newest. If a sector has thin material, say so in one line instead of padding it. Plain text, no markdown headers, no preamble about being an AI.

subject.title: Email subject
subject.description: Optional; defaults to Your weekly newsletter.

meeting-to-tickets.name: Meeting to tickets
meeting-to-tickets.description: Paste a meeting transcript. BOSS writes down what was decided and what somebody has to do, shows you the list, and creates the tickets once you approve.

transcript.title: Meeting transcript
transcript.description: Paste the notes or transcript to turn into actions.

video-workflow.name: Video edit and publish
video-workflow.description: Post a video link and say what you want done to it in plain English. A video agent does the editing with the skills it holds; a publishing agent waits for you before it uploads.

video_url.title: Video link
video_url.description: Optional. Google Drive share link, or any direct HTTPS link. Leave it blank and write the link into your instructions; the agent fetches whatever you point it at either way.

instructions.title: What you want done
instructions.description:
Plain English — say it the way you would to a person. The agent picks its own operations and their order from the skills it holds, so you describe the RESULT, not the steps.
It can keep a section, cut bits out of the middle, reframe to portrait or square, burn on a caption, put a picture on screen, add a logo, and join a title card or ending slide.
Timecodes: seconds, M:SS or HH:MM:SS. If your timecodes came off the original recording, say so — each operation applies to the result of the one before it.
Going landscape to portrait CROPS THE SIDES, so anything in a corner of the original — a channel badge, a logo — is cut off. To keep it, link the image above and say where it belongs.
If it needs something it was not given, it says so rather than guessing.
examples: Keep 3:42 to 4:50. Convert it to portrait for phones, taking the centre of the frame. The channel badge is already in the top corner — keep it exactly as it is. Put the ending slide on the end.

asset_url.title: Picture or clip
asset_url.description:
Optional. A link to a PICTURE or a short clip — ending slide, title card, logo, badge. Say in your instructions what it is for and the agent uses it accordingly: "put the ending slide on the end", "keep the channel badge in the top-right corner".
WORTH KNOWING: converting landscape to portrait crops the sides, so a logo or badge sitting in a corner of the original is cut off. If you want it kept, link the image here and say where it goes — the agent fetches it and puts it back.

title.title: YouTube title
title.description: Optional. Leave blank if your instructions point at a brief that contains it. The upload is PRIVATE either way, and YouTube refuses a video with no title, so the agent writes one from the brief if you have not.

description.title: YouTube description
description.description: Optional. Written in the brief, typed here, or left out.
